title: Optimizing Sequencing Resource Allocation
text: genomic surveillance, total number sequences can generate week fixed lab capacity budget. question many sequence (phylosamp answers ), distribute fixed number across regions, institutions, sample sources. Poor allocation wastes resources. sequence proportionally submissions (systems default), -represent regions send samples — often regions already highest sequencing rates.

title: Optimizing Sequencing Resource Allocation
text: survinger supports three optimization objectives: min_mse: Minimize mean squared error lineage prevalence estimates. Neyman-type allocation gives sequences high-variance strata. max_detection: Maximize probability detecting rare variant. spreads sequences maximize geographic coverage. min_imbalance: Minimize deviation population-proportional representation. ensures region fairly represented.

title: Delay-Adjusted Nowcasting
text: sample collection sequence upload, delay typically 1–4 weeks. means look latest data, recent weeks always incomplete — fewer people infected, results arrived yet. ignore plot raw counts, see false decline recent weeks. called right-truncation bias.

title: Delay-Adjusted Nowcasting
text: survinger fits parametric delay distribution accounting fact can observe delays shorter time elapsed since collection (right-truncation correction).
code: library(survinger) data(sarscov2_surveillance)  design <- surv_design(   data = sarscov2_surveillance$sequences,   strata = ~ region,   sequencing_rate = sarscov2_surveillance$population[c("region", "seq_rate")],   population = sarscov2_surveillance$population )  delay_fit <- surv_estimate_delay(design, distribution = "negbin") print(delay_fit) #> ── Reporting Delay Distribution ──────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Distribution: "negbin" #> Strata: none (pooled) #> Observations: 1349 #> Mean delay: 9.9 days #>  #> # A tibble: 1 × 5 #>   stratum distribution    mu  size converged #>   <chr>   <chr>        <dbl> <dbl> <lgl>     #> 1 all     negbin        9.95  3.52 TRUE plot(delay_fit)

title: Delay-Adjusted Nowcasting
text: Given fitted delay, can ask: fraction sequences collected d days ago reported now? Sequences collected 7 days ago may partially reported, 28 days ago nearly complete.
code: days <- c(7, 14, 21, 28) probs <- surv_reporting_probability(delay_fit, delta = days) data.frame(days_ago = days, prob_reported = round(probs, 3)) #>   days_ago prob_reported #> 1        7         0.403 #> 2       14         0.797 #> 3       21         0.949 #> 4       28         0.989

title: Delay-Adjusted Nowcasting

code: nowcast <- surv_nowcast_lineage(design, delay_fit, "BA.2.86") plot(nowcast)

title: Introduction to survinger
text: Pathogen genomic surveillance backbone pandemic preparedness. sequencing positive samples tracking lineage frequencies time, public health agencies can detect emerging variants early monitor spread. However, real-world surveillance systems fundamental bias problem: sequencing rates highly unequal across regions institutions. well-resourced capital city might sequence 15% positive cases, rural area sequences 0.5%. simply count uploaded sequences estimate “fraction variant X?”, answer dominated high-sequencing regions — regardless actually circulating elsewhere. top , reporting delay problem. sample collection sequence upload, 1–4 weeks can pass. means recent weeks data always incomplete, naive trend estimates systematically undercount latest period. survinger addresses problems unified framework.

code: library(survinger)  # Simulate surveillance data (or use your own) sim <- surv_simulate(n_regions = 5, n_weeks = 26, seed = 42)  # Create design from surveillance data design <- surv_design(   data = sim$sequences, strata = ~ region,   sequencing_rate = sim$population[c("region", "seq_rate")],   population = sim$population )  # Corrected prevalence (one line) surv_lineage_prevalence(design, "BA.2.86")  # Or even simpler — single pipe-friendly call: surv_estimate(   data = sim$sequences, strata = ~ region,   sequencing_rate = sim$population[c("region", "seq_rate")],   population = sim$population, lineage = "BA.2.86" )  # Full pipeline with delay correction delay <- surv_estimate_delay(design) surv_adjusted_prevalence(design, delay, "BA.2.86")  # How should I allocate 500 sequences? surv_optimize_allocation(design, "min_mse", total_capacity = 500)  # Is my system powerful enough? surv_detection_probability(design, true_prevalence = 0.01)  # One-page diagnostic surv_report(design)

Core functions: surv_design(), surv_optimize_allocation(), surv_lineage_prevalence(), surv_estimate_delay(), surv_nowcast_lineage(), surv_adjusted_prevalence(), surv_detection_probability(), surv_required_sequences().
